title: Is there a name for this kind of shot?

commenti.body:
This scene is a combination of setups and shots, there’s no one term for it. I would most simply describe it as an aerial tracking shot that cuts to an over the shoulder POV shot. 

If this were made today I would imagine the camera attached to a drone would seamlessly track and push all the way into the backseat of car using CGI to mask the cuts.

I'm not sure there is a particular name for the technique but I've heard people call it a "POV fallacy". Antonioni did it a lot. And Wim Wenders also uses it in The American Friend.

"POV fallacy", that sounds good! Yeah, I remember seeing it in Antonioni, but I couldn't find a specific example, just vaguely remember it happening. I'm gonna check the Wenders one, I haven't seen it. Thanks a lot!
That's interesting because I hadn't thought about it being a choice made because of technical constraints, but could be in some cases.

Great question! There should be a name, I’ve seen people discuss it online before. I think Todd Vaziri tweeted about it like 10 years ago. FYI The end of 2001 has famous instance of a character entering their own POV. It’s purposely jarring.

>The end of 2001

Right! You mean the sequence [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4UkjVk03sIk) that starts at around 2:44, right? That's insane; it's kinda like what I mean but without leaving the first POV entirely, but it's still unsettling, or actually even more so. 

I didn't know about Todd Vaziri, I'm having fun checking his tweets. Thank you!
